events.name: Thieving bat
versions: A bat swooped down and snatched a shiny coin from his purse.
A cheeky bat flew off with one of his coins.
quiet: A bat swooped at his purse, found it empty and flew off in a huff.
A bat looked for something shiny on him, found nothing and gave up.
quietThoughts: Shoo, bat. My purse is empty.

events.name: Coins in a crack
versions: He found three coins hidden in a crack in the wall.
Something glinted in a crack in the wall: three old coins.

events.name: Friendly ghost
events.deed: a friendly ghost gave him a torch
versions: A friendly ghost floated up and handed him a torch.
A shy little ghost gave him a torch and vanished with a giggle.
quiet: A friendly ghost offered him a torch, but his pack was full, so it floated away.
A ghost held out a torch, saw his full pack and shrugged.
thoughts: A ghost with a torch? Thanks!
Boo to you too. Nice torch.
quietThoughts: No room for that torch, ghost.

events.name: Cold spring
events.deed: a drink from a cold spring
versions: He drank from a cold spring and felt better.
A cold spring bubbled up from the floor, and a sip made him feel stronger.
quiet: He found a cold spring, but he felt fine already.
He splashed his face at a cold spring and walked on.
thoughts: A spring! Just what I needed.

events.name: Gust of wind
events.deed: a gust of wind made his torch burn low
versions: A gust of wind blew through the tunnel, and his torch burned low.
A cold wind howled down the passage and nearly blew his torch out.
quiet: A cold gust blew through the tunnel, but he had no torch burning.
The wind howled down the passage and ruffled his hair.

events.name: Bat colony
versions: Hundreds of bats hung from the ceiling, fast asleep.
A cloud of bats woke up, circled once and went back to sleep.

events.name: Dripping echo
versions: Drip… drip… drip… the echo went on and on.
Water dripped somewhere, and the echo made it sound like a drum.

events.name: Old skeleton
versions: An old skeleton told him a joke. It was very dry.
An old skeleton asked him why it never fights anyone. It has no guts!
An old skeleton waved at him and went back to its nap.
thoughts: A talking skeleton. Sure. Why not.

events.name: Spider weaving
versions: A spider was weaving a web across the tunnel, so he ducked under it.
A spider waved four of its legs at him and went on weaving.

events.name: Glowing mushrooms
versions: Blue mushrooms glowed softly in a corner.
He found a ring of glowing mushrooms and stepped carefully around it.

events.name: Rumble below
versions: The floor rumbled, as if something big turned over in its sleep.
A deep rumble came from far below, then all was quiet.

events.name: Rats behind the wall
versions: Rats squeaked and scrabbled behind the wall.
He heard tiny feet running behind the stones.

events.name: Carved warning
versions: Someone had carved "Turn back!" into the wall. He did not.
Big letters on the wall said "Beware of the big one".

events.name: Empty chest
versions: He found a big old chest. It was empty, except for a moth.
He opened a chest with a creak, and found only dust.
thoughts: Who empties a chest and leaves it?

events.name: Goblin's lost sock
versions: He found a goblin's lost sock. It smelled terrible.
A single green sock lay on the floor, with a hole in the toe.

events.name: Dragon's snore
versions: Far, far away, a dragon snored. He decided not to look.
A snore as loud as thunder came from somewhere very deep.
thoughts: Was that a dragon? Let it sleep.

events.name: Sword in a stone
versions: A rusty sword was stuck in a stone. He pulled. It stayed.
He found a sword stuck in a stone, and it would not budge.

events.name: Hero paintings
versions: Old paintings on the wall showed a hero who looked a bit like him.
Faded paintings showed a hero fighting a troll. The troll was winning.

events.name: Dwarf's lunch
versions: A dwarf had left his lunch box behind: one old cheese sandwich.
He found a dwarf's lunch box with a note: "Back at noon".

events.name: Draught from the stairs
versions: A cold draught came down the stairs from the world above.
He could smell fresh air coming down the stairs.
thoughts: Fresh air. The stairs are close.

events.name: Keeper's notice
versions: A notice on the wall said: "Gate closes at sundown. No exceptions."
A notice from the keeper said: "Please wipe your boots."

events.name: Snoring guard
versions: Something big was snoring nearby.
He heard heavy breathing from somewhere close.

events.name: Loose stone
versions: A floor stone clicked under his boot. Nothing happened.
A loose stone wobbled under his foot, and he froze. Just a stone.

events.name: Chalk arrow
versions: Someone had drawn a chalk arrow on the floor, and the word "Ouch".
Chalk marks on the floor said "Watch your step".

events.name: Glowworms
versions: Glowworms lit the ceiling like tiny stars.
A line of glowworms showed him the way for a while.

events.name: Echo
versions: He shouted "Hello!" and the echo shouted back "Go home!"
He hummed a tune, and the echo hummed it back, a little off.

events.name: Puddle
versions: He stepped into a deep puddle. Splash!
His boot sank into a cold puddle up to the ankle.

events.name: Painted door
versions: A door was painted on the wall at the end of the tunnel. He knocked anyway.
He found a painted door. Nobody answered.

events.name: Lost mole
versions: A lost mole popped out of the floor, sniffed, and popped back in.
A mole asked him the way to the top. He pointed up.

troll: That troll hits like a tree.

light: Torch on. Now I see you.

pickUp: Nothing here to pick up. Hmph.

openings: Hear the saga of the raid on dungeon {code}!
Down the stairs of dungeon {code} went the barbarian.
Once, the barbarian went down into dungeon {code}.
Listen! The barbarian entered dungeon {code}, axe in hand.
beatenOne: A {monster} stood in his way, and soon it was a little pile of coins.
He beat a {monster}, and it turned into coins.
beatenMany: He beat {n} {monsters}, and each turned into coins.
{N} {monsters} met his axe and turned into coins.
hits: A {monster} hit him hard, but he kept going.
He took a blow from a {monster} and grumbled.
trap: He stepped on a spike trap. Ouch!
Spikes jumped out of the floor and poked his feet.
picked: He picked up {gold} gold along the way.
He filled his purse with {gold} gold.
digOne: A wall stood in his way, so he knocked it down.
potionOne: He drank a potion and felt better.
torch: He lit a torch, and the shadows ran.
His torch lit up the dark.
strength: He found strength, and hit harder from then on.
vigour: He found vigour, and felt tougher from then on.

left: Then he climbed the stairs into the daylight and carried out {gold} gold.
And he walked out by the stairs with {gold} gold.
leftNoGold: Then he climbed back up the stairs with empty pockets.
And he walked out by the stairs, carrying out no gold at all.
knockedOut: Then he was knocked out, and the dungeon keeper carried him out. He carried out no gold.
But at last he was knocked out, and the keeper carried him up the stairs. Not a coin came with him.
lockedIn: Then the sun went down and the gate closed. The keeper let him out in the morning and kept all the gold.
But he was too late: the gate closed at sundown, and the keeper kept every coin.

hits: A {monster} hit him {big} times, and he only laughed.
He took {big} blows from a {monster} without a scratch.
trap: He stepped on {big} spike traps and did not even notice.
dig: He smashed through {big} walls with his bare hands!
{Big} walls crumbled when he looked at them.

fantasy: He wrestled a dragon and won.
A talking door asked him a riddle, and he answered with a song.
He rode a giant snail through a tunnel of crystals.
The dungeon walls sang him a battle song.
A tiny wizard turned his boots into frogs, then back again.
He arm-wrestled a stone giant to a draw.
He found a lake under the ground and swam across it with one breath.
A troll king asked him for advice and took it.
He tamed a cave bear, and it carried him for a while.
The moon shone into the dungeon, just for him.
